name: UI Implementation - Core Flows
one_line_goal: Turn the stub screens into a genuinely usable local-only app, backed by the real data layer and the real engine.
objective: Build every core user flow - onboarding, add income with preview and override, category and account management, dashboard, spending log and business scope - wired to real local data.
rationale: This is the first stage where the app becomes usable, and the last chance to find that a design decision does not survive contact with a real screen. Sync deliberately comes after it.
entry_criteria: The distribution engine passes all golden vectors and property tests.
The data layer is green and seeded defaults are valid.
NAVIGATION.md screen inventory and per-screen states are approved.

how_to_work_this_stage.unit_of_work: One substage per working session. Work them strictly in listed order; do not parallelise or skip.
how_to_work_this_stage.between_substages: Tick the substage off, append evidence to docs/reports/STAGE_6_WORKLOG.md, then start the next. No user approval needed between substages.
how_to_work_this_stage.at_stage_end: The final substage assembles the stage report and stops for user approval before the next stage file is opened.
substage_list: 6.1 App shell, state wiring and scope switching
6.2 Onboarding part one: currency, scope and top-level split
6.3 Onboarding part two: categories, percentages, ceilings and accounts
6.4 Add income form and live allocation preview
6.11 Cross-cutting UI quality: states, inputs and accessibility
6.12 Widget tests, flow tests and offline verification

substages.name: App shell, state wiring and scope switching
substages.goal: Connect the presentation layer to use cases and repositories, and implement the personal and business scope switch.
substages.why_it_matters: Every subsequent substage builds on this plumbing; getting it wrong once costs eleven substages of rework.
entry_criteria: The distribution engine passes all golden vectors and property tests.
The data layer is green and seeded defaults are valid.
NAVIGATION.md screen inventory and per-screen states are approved.

work.action: Set up dependency injection so screens receive use cases, and use cases receive repository interfaces and the engine.
details: No widget may construct a repository or call the database directly.
Add a check or review rule that enforces this.

work.action: Implement the use case layer for the flows this stage builds: complete onboarding, preview allocation, confirm income, reverse income, save category, save account, log spending.
details: A use case orchestrates; it does not contain allocation arithmetic.
Each use case returns a typed result the UI can map to a message.

work.action: Wire reactive repository streams into the state layer so any database change reaches the UI.
details: Test it by mutating from a different code path and asserting the screen updates.

work.action: Implement the scope switch decided in Stage 2, with the state that tracks the active scope.
details: Include the personal-only case: no business surface, no dead navigation, no empty group.

work.action: Implement app startup: read settings, decide whether to route to onboarding or dashboard, and handle the not-yet-seeded case.
Implement the global error surface used by every screen for typed failures, so error handling is not reinvented twelve times.
Confirm the app still launches and every route is reachable after the rewiring.

acceptance_criteria: No widget constructs a repository or touches the database directly.
A change made through a non-UI code path updates the visible screen, proven by a test.
A personal-only configuration shows no business surface anywhere.
Startup routes correctly for a fresh install, a mid-onboarding install and a completed install.
The global error surface renders a typed failure with a specific message.
must_not: Do not put allocation arithmetic in a use case.
Do not let a widget call a repository.
common_pitfalls: Screens that each invent their own error handling, producing twelve inconsistent messages.
A scope switch implemented per screen rather than centrally, so one screen forgets it.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

substages.name: Onboarding part one: currency, scope and top-level split
substages.goal: Build the first three onboarding steps with an exact-100-percent constraint that cannot be violated.
substages.why_it_matters: NFR-04 and R-06. This is where a first-time budgeter is won or lost, and where an invalid configuration would poison everything after it.
entry_criteria: Substage 6.1 (App shell, state wiring and scope switching) is complete and ticked off.

work.action: Step 1, welcome and currency.
details: Detect from device locale, show the detected currency and let the user change it.
State in one plain sentence that it cannot be changed once transactions exist (OQ-01).
Store the ISO code and minor unit exponent in settings.

work.action: Step 2, scope selection: personal only, or personal plus business.
details: Choosing personal only hides the business group entirely rather than showing an empty one.
State that it can be enabled later, and make sure that is true.

work.action: Step 3, top-level split across Spending, Savings and Business.
details: Use a control that makes submitting anything other than exactly 100 percent impossible.
Show the live remainder as the user drags or types, so the constraint is visible rather than punitive.
Provide a sensible default that the user can accept immediately.
Convert to basis points on save and validate the total is exactly 10000.

work.action: Implement progress persistence so a killed app resumes at the same step with data intact.
Implement Android back through these steps without losing entered data.
Implement the skip-to-defaults path from step 3, and verify it produces a valid configuration.
Write widget tests for the exact-100-percent constraint, including attempts to submit 99 and 101 percent.

acceptance_criteria: It is impossible to leave step 3 with a split that is not exactly 10000 basis points.
Killing the app mid-onboarding and reopening resumes at the same step with data intact.
Back navigation preserves entered data at every step.
The skip-to-defaults path produces a configuration that passes every validator.
The whole flow completes with no network connection.
must_not: Do not allow the user to proceed with an invalid split and fix it later.
Do not require a network connection or a Google account.
common_pitfalls: A percentage control that permits 99 percent and shows an error only on submit.
Onboarding state held only in memory, lost when Android reclaims the process.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

substages.name: Onboarding part two: categories, percentages, ceilings and accounts
substages.goal: Build the remaining onboarding steps so a first-time user leaves with a valid, personal configuration.
substages.why_it_matters: FR-08 - suggestions must be genuinely editable, and the whole path must remain completable in under two minutes by accepting defaults.
entry_criteria: Substage 6.2 (Onboarding part one: currency, scope and top-level split) is complete and ticked off.

work.action: Step 4, categories: present the seeded suggestions pre-selected, each editable and removable inline, with an obvious add-custom action.
details: Show the suggested type for each and let the user change it.
Group them visibly by Spending, Savings and Business.

work.action: Step 5, within-group percentages: the same exact-100-percent constraint per group.
details: Provide a one-tap split evenly action as an escape hatch.
Recompute automatically when a category is added or removed, rather than leaving the user with an invalid total.

work.action: Step 6, optional ceilings: let the user set a ceiling and redirect target for accumulating categories.
details: Make skipping obvious and consequence-free, leaving them uncapped.
The redirect target picker must exclude choices that would create a cycle, computed live.

work.action: Step 7, optional accounts: add bank accounts and link them to categories, fully skippable.
details: State plainly that these are labels and the app does not connect to any bank.

work.action: Step 8, done: land on the dashboard with a single prompt to add the first income.
Verify the sink category exists and is reachable as a redirect target, and explain it in one line where it first appears.
Time the full default-accepting path on a device and record it.
Write a flow test covering the accept-everything path from launch to dashboard.

acceptance_criteria: Every seeded category can be renamed, retyped, re-ceilinged or removed during onboarding.
Adding or removing a category leaves the group percentages valid, never invalid.
The redirect target picker cannot offer a choice that creates a cycle, proven by a widget test.
The accept-everything path completes in under 2 minutes, timed and recorded.
Onboarding finishes with a configuration that passes every validator.
must_not: Do not make any suggestion mandatory.
Do not require ceilings or accounts to finish onboarding.
common_pitfalls: Removing a category and leaving the group at 85 percent with no prompt.
A cycle-creating redirect target offered in the picker and rejected only on save.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

substages.name: Add income form and live allocation preview
substages.goal: Build the income entry form with a live, explained allocation preview computed by the engine.
substages.why_it_matters: FR-04. This is the moment the app delivers its core value, and the moment the user decides whether to trust it.
entry_criteria: Substage 6.3 (Onboarding part two: categories, percentages, ceilings and accounts) is complete and ticked off.
inputs: Stage 5 engine entry point and diagnostics trace.

work.action: Build the entry form: amount, source label, date, optional note, and for a business-enabled user the personal or business income toggle if that was the agreed model.
details: Use the money input widget so an invalid amount cannot be entered.

work.action: Call the engine on every amount change and render the preview.
details: Every category, its allocated amount, its resulting balance, and its progress toward its ceiling.
Debounce so typing stays smooth on a mid-tier device, but never so long that the preview feels detached from the keystroke.

work.action: Render the diagnostics trace as plain-language explanations, not developer output.
details: For example: a category is full, so a stated amount moved to a named category instead.
Every hop the engine reports must be visible to the user in some form, at least on expansion.

work.action: Show the running total against the entered amount at all times, so conservation is visible (INV-02).
Handle every engine typed failure with a specific message and a way forward.
details: Zero or negative amount, amount above the maximum, invalid configuration, missing sink.
A configuration failure should route the user to the screen that fixes it.

work.action: Ensure the preview never performs any allocation arithmetic itself - it renders the engine's output only.
details: Add a review rule or a test asserting the preview and the confirmed write produce identical figures.

work.action: Handle the empty and loading states: no categories configured, and the brief moment before the first computation.

acceptance_criteria: The preview total always equals the entered amount, tested at 1 minor unit, typical values and near the documented maximum.
Every redirect the engine reports is explained in words a non-technical user understands.
The preview performs no arithmetic of its own, proven by a test comparing preview output to engine output.
Every typed failure produces a specific message and a route forward.
Typing remains smooth on a mid-tier device with 40 categories configured.
must_not: Do not compute any part of the split in the widget layer.
Do not hide a redirect from the user.
common_pitfalls: A preview that rounds for display in a way that makes the visible total disagree with the entered amount.
Diagnostics rendered as raw developer text.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

substages.name: Manual override, confirmation and undo
substages.goal: Let the user adjust a single income event, confirm it atomically, and undo it cleanly.
substages.why_it_matters: FR-12 and INV-03 - the user must be able to bend the rules for one payment, and to correct a mistake without history lying about it.
entry_criteria: Substage 6.4 (Add income form and live allocation preview) is complete and ticked off.

work.action: Implement per-category inline override editing within the preview.
details: As the user overrides one category, redistribute the rest live via the engine and keep the total exact.
Show clearly which categories are overridden and which are computed.

work.action: Disable confirmation whenever the overridden total does not equal the income exactly, and state why in place.
details: Never allow a confirm that would break conservation.

work.action: Show a warning where an override pushes a category past its ceiling, per the Stage 2 policy, without blocking it.
Implement confirm: write the income event and every allocation in a single atomic transaction.
details: Guard against double submission - a rapid double tap must not create two events.
Use the client-generated UUID so a retry is idempotent.

work.action: Implement the success state summarising what happened, including any redirects, with a direct undo action.
Implement undo via the reversal path, and confirm balances return exactly to their pre-event values.
details: Show the reversal in history rather than making the event disappear.

work.action: Implement reversal from the history screen too, not only from the immediate success state.
Write flow tests for override, confirm, undo, and rapid double-tap.

acceptance_criteria: Confirmation is impossible unless the total equals the income exactly.
Confirming writes exactly one income event with allocations summing exactly to the income, verified by reading the database.
A rapid double tap creates exactly one event, proven by a test.
A partially failed write leaves no rows behind, proven by a test.
Undo returns every balance exactly and leaves both the event and its reversal visible in history.
must_not: Do not allow confirmation of a non-conserving total.
Do not make a reversed event disappear from history.
common_pitfalls: Double submission from an un-debounced confirm button, which duplicates income silently.
Undo implemented as a delete, which violates the append-only ledger.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

substages.name: Category management
substages.goal: Give the user full control over categories, types, percentages, ceilings and redirect targets, without ever permitting an invalid configuration.
substages.why_it_matters: FR-01, FR-10 and FR-11 - this is the user's control surface over their own money model.
entry_criteria: Substage 6.5 (Manual override, confirmation and undo) is complete and ticked off.

work.action: Build the category list grouped by category group, with the business group visually distinct.
Build create and edit: name, group, type, percentage within group, ceiling or bill amount and anchor day, redirect target, linked account, sort order.
Enforce the exact-100-percent rule when a percentage changes.
details: Either require explicit rebalancing of siblings, or offer automatic proportional rebalancing with a preview of exactly what will change.
Never save a configuration that fails validation, and never leave the user stuck with an invalid state they cannot exit.

work.action: Build the redirect target picker that excludes the category itself and any choice creating a cycle, computed live.
Implement archive rather than delete for categories with ledger history, and explain the difference in one line.
details: A category with history can never be hard-deleted without destroying the audit trail.

work.action: Block archiving a category that is another category's redirect target or that is the sink, naming the dependant in the message.
Build the category detail screen showing current balance, ceiling progress, redirect destination and recent activity.
Warn clearly when a rule change will alter future allocations, and confirm that history is unaffected.
Write widget tests for the cycle-free picker, the percentage constraint and the archive guards.

acceptance_criteria: The redirect picker cannot offer a cycle-creating option, proven against an adversarial configuration.
Saving with group percentages other than exactly 100 percent is blocked with a specific message.
Archiving a category with history preserves every ledger entry and reports still reconcile.
Archiving a redirect target or the sink is blocked and names the dependant.
Changing a percentage does not alter any past income event's allocations, proven by a test.
outputs: Category list, edit and detail screens.
must_not: Do not offer hard delete for a category with ledger history.
Do not let the UI be the only enforcer of a validation rule.
common_pitfalls: Auto-rebalancing that silently changes percentages the user set deliberately.
An archive action that orphans a redirect target, breaking the next allocation.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

substages.name: Account management
substages.goal: Let the user record which real-world account holds which categories, without implying bank connectivity.
substages.why_it_matters: FR-03 - the user needs to know where the money physically sits, and must never think the app is reading their bank.
entry_criteria: Substage 6.6 (Category management) is complete and ticked off.

work.action: Build the account list with name, institution, optional last four digits, and the derived total of linked categories.
Build create and edit, with a clear statement that these are labels and the app does not connect to any bank.
details: If OQ-02 resolved toward real balances, implement that model instead and state it here.

work.action: Support linking many categories to one account, and show the linked categories from the account detail.
Handle deletion of an account with linked categories: require explicit reassignment or unlinking, never orphan silently.
Build the informational reconciliation view: expected total versus what the user says the bank shows.
details: Purely informational; no automatic adjustment, no implication of a live feed.

work.action: Write tests asserting per-account totals equal the sum of linked category balances.

acceptance_criteria: Per-account totals equal the sum of linked category balances, verified against ledger-derived values.
Deleting an account with links is impossible without explicit reassignment.
No screen implies live bank connectivity.
An account with no linked categories renders a clear empty state.
outputs: Account list, edit and detail screens.
must_not: Do not imply the app reads bank data.
Do not orphan a category by deleting its account.
common_pitfalls: Wording such as connect your bank, which sets an expectation the app cannot meet.
Account totals computed from a cached value rather than the ledger.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

substages.name: Dashboard
substages.goal: Build the screen the user opens most, with every figure derived from the ledger and updating reactively.
substages.why_it_matters: FR-13 - one wrong number here loses the user's trust in everything else.
entry_criteria: Substage 6.7 (Account management) is complete and ticked off.
inputs: Stage 4 reactive queries and balance derivation.

work.action: Show group-level totals for Spending, Savings and Business with clear separation.
Show each category with balance, ceiling and progress indicator, in the user's sort order, with an option to sort by fullness.
Highlight categories that are full and therefore redirecting, and name where their money is going.
details: This turns the app's signature behaviour from a surprise into a feature.

work.action: Show recent income events and spending transactions with a link into history.
Drive every figure from reactive queries so the screen updates when data changes underneath, including from a future background sync.
Implement the empty state for a user who finished onboarding but logged nothing, with a single obvious action.
Implement the loading and error states designed in Stage 2.
Add pull-to-refresh that recomputes derived balances, and leave a hook for triggering sync in Stage 7.
Test the dashboard against the five-year synthetic dataset for both correctness and render performance.

acceptance_criteria: Every displayed balance equals the ledger-derived value, proven by a test comparing rendered figures to a recomputation.
The dashboard renders within the NFR-06 budget with the five-year dataset loaded.
Adding an income event from another screen updates the dashboard without a manual refresh.
Full categories are visibly marked and name their redirect destination.
The empty state offers exactly one obvious next action.
must_not: Do not display a figure from a cached counter without the derivation path behind it.
Do not require a refresh to show a change made elsewhere in the app.
common_pitfalls: A dashboard that loads everything eagerly and stutters at realistic data volume.
Progress indicators that show 100 percent before a category is genuinely full, due to display rounding.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

substages.name: Spending log and transaction history
substages.goal: Let money leave categories, and make every past movement inspectable and correctable.
substages.why_it_matters: Balances only mean something if spending is recorded, and corrections must not rewrite history.
entry_criteria: Substage 6.8 (Dashboard) is complete and ticked off.

work.action: Build quick spending entry: amount, category, account, date, note.
details: Offer the most recently used categories first, since speed matters at the point of purchase.
Default the account from the category's link.

work.action: Apply the OQ-06 policy for spending that takes a category negative.
details: Warn prominently, explain the consequence, but do not block the user from recording reality.

work.action: Write spending as immutable ledger entries; an edit becomes a compensating entry plus a new entry.
details: Show the correction in history rather than replacing the original.

work.action: Build the history screen with filters by date range, group, category and account, plus running balances.
Show reversals, corrections and redirects explicitly, so nothing ever appears to vanish.
Scope the pickers so business categories never appear in personal spending and vice versa.
Implement pagination or lazy loading so history performs at the five-year data volume.
Write tests for the correction path and for scope isolation.

acceptance_criteria: Editing a spending entry leaves the original visible in history alongside its correction.
A personal spending entry cannot be assigned to a business category through any path in the UI.
History filters produce totals that reconcile with the dashboard for the same period.
History renders and scrolls within budget at the five-year volume.
Spending that takes a category negative warns clearly and still records.
must_not: Do not mutate a ledger entry in place.
Do not block a user from recording a real transaction.
common_pitfalls: An edit implemented as delete-and-reinsert, which destroys the audit trail.
Loading the entire history into memory to compute running balances.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

substages.name: Business scope separation
substages.goal: Make business money impossible to confuse with household money, everywhere in the app.
substages.why_it_matters: FR-07 and NFR-03 - business float spent on groceries is precisely the failure persona P2 fears.
entry_criteria: Substage 6.9 (Spending log and transaction history) is complete and ticked off.

work.action: Apply the scope separation consistently across dashboard, spending, categories, accounts and history.
details: One mechanism, applied centrally, not re-implemented per screen.

work.action: Apply the distinct visual treatment from the theme, and verify it in dark mode and in greyscale.
details: Meaning must not depend on colour alone (NFR-08).

work.action: Ensure personal totals never silently include business figures anywhere, including summary cards.
details: Any combined figure must be explicitly labelled as combined.

work.action: Handle the personal-only user: no business UI, no empty business group, no dead navigation, and a clear path to enabling it later.
Handle enabling business after onboarding: seed the business categories, require the group percentages to be rebalanced to exactly 100 percent, and guide the user through it.
Write a test that walks every screen and asserts no unlabelled figure mixes scopes.

acceptance_criteria: No screen shows a combined personal-plus-business total unless explicitly labelled as combined.
A personal-only user sees no business surface anywhere.
Enabling business later produces a valid configuration and guides the rebalancing.
The visual distinction is legible in both themes and in greyscale.
The cross-screen scope test passes.
must_not: Do not implement scope filtering separately on each screen.
Do not convey scope by colour alone.
common_pitfalls: One summary card that quietly sums all groups, undoing the separation everywhere else.
Enabling business later leaving the group split at 100 percent across only two groups.

substages.name: Cross-cutting UI quality: states, inputs and accessibility
substages.goal: Give every screen its three states, a safe money input, and accessibility built in rather than retrofitted.
substages.why_it_matters: It is far cheaper to build these in now than to audit twenty finished screens in Stage 10.
entry_criteria: Substage 6.10 (Business scope separation) is complete and ticked off.

work.action: Implement the empty, loading and error state for every screen as designed, with no exceptions.
details: Walk the screen inventory and tick each one; a screen without all three is not finished.

work.action: Implement the money input widget.
details: Accepts only valid amounts for the configured currency, with the correct number of decimal places.
Rejects invalid paste content rather than silently truncating it.
Produces an integer minor-unit value and never a floating point number.
Handles the currency exponent, including 0 and 3.

work.action: Add semantic labels for screen readers on every interactive element as it is built.
details: Money amounts must be announced in a form that makes sense read aloud, not as raw digits.

work.action: Verify each screen at 200 percent font scale as it is completed, rather than at the end.
Add confirmation dialogs for destructive and irreversible actions, and ensure nothing destructive is one accidental tap away.
Keep every user-facing string in one place, ready for localisation.
Verify minimum touch target sizes and logical focus order across the app.

acceptance_criteria: No screen lacks an empty, loading or error state.
The money input cannot produce an invalid amount, including through paste, proven by tests.
Every screen remains usable at 200 percent font scale with no clipped or overlapping text.
Every interactive element has a screen-reader label.
No user-facing string is hardcoded inside a widget's logic.
must_not: Do not defer accessibility labels to Stage 9 or 10.
Do not hardcode two decimal places in the input.
common_pitfalls: A money input that accepts a pasted value with four decimals and rounds it silently.
Font scaling checked once at the end, when fixing it means relaying out every screen.

substages.name: Widget tests, flow tests and offline verification
substages.goal: Test every screen and every core journey, and prove the whole app works with no network.
substages.why_it_matters: Stage 9 is a QA pass, not the first time anything is tested. And NFR-02 is only real if it is demonstrated.
entry_criteria: Substage 6.11 (Cross-cutting UI quality: states, inputs and accessibility) is complete and ticked off.

work.action: Write widget tests for each screen covering its empty, populated and error states.
Write a flow test for onboarding through to a confirmed first income event.
Write a flow test for hitting a ceiling and seeing the redirect explained in the preview.
Write a flow test for override, confirm and undo, asserting balances return exactly.
Write a flow test for the business scope: log business income and spending, and assert personal totals are unaffected.
Run every flow in an offline configuration with no network permission and no account linked.
details: This is the demonstration of NFR-02; capture the evidence for the stage report.

work.action: Assert on underlying data in each flow test, not only on rendered widgets, so a display bug and a data bug are distinguishable.
Measure and record presentation layer coverage, naming any gaps.
Time the first-time user path end to end and record it against the 5 minute NFR-04 target.
Write docs/UI_NOTES.md and docs/reports/STAGE_6_REPORT.md, and prepare the gate.

acceptance_criteria: All widget and flow tests pass, with output captured.
Every core flow completes offline with no account linked, with evidence recorded.
Each flow test asserts on ledger state as well as on widgets.
Presentation layer coverage is at least 70 percent with named gaps.
The first-time user path is timed and meets the 5 minute target.
must_not: Do not skip the offline run - it is the evidence for NFR-02.
Do not assert only on rendered text for money-moving flows.
common_pitfalls: Flow tests that pass because they assert on the same computed value the screen displays.
Offline verification done on a device that still has cached credentials, which hides a dependency.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

checkpoint.action: Final substage. Assemble the stage report, then STOP and request approval using approval_gate.question_to_user below.
escalate_immediately_if: A core flow cannot complete offline - this contradicts NFR-02 and must be raised before the gate.

stage_definition_of_done: Every core flow is completable end to end on a real device with no network connection.
Every figure shown in the UI is derived from the ledger, never from a hand-maintained counter.
All widget and flow tests pass.
A first-time user can complete onboarding and their first income split in under 5 minutes.
Business and personal data are separated everywhere.
TRACEABILITY.md updated for every requirement this stage completes.
stage_must_not: Do not implement cloud sync, Google Sign-In or any network call in this stage.
Do not duplicate any allocation logic in the UI; the engine is the only place that computes a split.
Do not mutate balances directly from a screen.
Do not leave a screen without its empty, loading and error states.
Do not use placeholder content in anything a reviewer might mistake for finished work.
Do not add analytics, crash reporting or any SDK that transmits data off-device.
anti_patterns: Recomputing a split in the widget layer for the preview, which then diverges from what confirmation writes.
An onboarding flow so thorough that a first-time user abandons it.
Showing a redirect as a bare number with no explanation, which reads as money going missing.
Deferring accessibility labels to Stage 10, where they become an audit instead of a habit.

artifacts_next_stage_consumes: A complete, correct local app that Stage 7 makes multi-device without changing its behaviour.
Reactive queries throughout, so background sync updates the UI with no extra plumbing.
The sync status surface, stubbed and ready for Stage 7 to drive.
handoff.summary_to_write: Confirm every core flow works offline and list anything intentionally deferred to Stage 10 polish.

approval_gate.question_to_user: Stage 6 (Core UI) is complete. The app is fully usable offline: onboarding, income splitting with preview and override, categories, accounts, dashboard, spending and business scope. Deferred polish items: <list>. Do you approve moving to Stage 7, cloud sync?
